claims.text: The initial material is nanocrystalline CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy.
The nanocrystalline CoCrFeMnNi material is produced by high-pressure torsion.
An approach integrating ab initio phonon calculations and grain-boundary scattering models can accurately identify high-entropy alloys with exceptionally low phonon thermal conductivity.
The approach works in the nanocrystalline regime because it captures enhanced scattering at numerous grain boundaries.
High-pressure torsion followed by annealing at 600°C can maintain grain sizes below 1 μm.
A nanocrystalline microstructure has enhanced grain-boundary density.
A high density of grain boundaries introduces additional phonon-scattering centers.
Grain-boundary scattering reduces the phonon mean free path.
Combining intrinsic lattice-vibrational behavior with extrinsic boundary effects should improve thermal-conductivity predictions over conventional models.
For grain sizes below 1 μm, lattice thermal conductivity will be at least 20% lower than in comparable coarse-grained samples.
For grain sizes below 1 μm, model prediction errors will remain within 20%.
For grain sizes above 1 μm, model predictions will deviate from measurements by more than 20%.
Current predictive models generally omit detailed grain-boundary scattering effects and are intended for coarse-grained samples.
Current predictive models predict higher thermal conductivity values than the proposed approach.
The proposed approach is valid only for nanocrystalline systems with grain sizes below 1 μm.
At grain sizes above 1 μm, other scattering mechanisms may dominate and cause the model to fail.
Grain-boundary scattering is a well-established phonon-scattering mechanism.
Contributions from distinct phonon-scattering sources should be integrated rather than simply overlapped.
